name: relative_strength_momentum_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: Stocks showing the strongest intraday returns relative to their sector peers in the first 60 minutes tend to continue outperforming for the next 2-3 hours. This is driven by information asymmetry — when one stock in a sector moves first, institutional flow follows into that specific name. The leader-follower dynamic creates persistent momentum in the relative outperformer. Edge persists because computing real-time sector-relative strength across 200+ stocks requires infrastructure most retail traders don't have.
stock_filter: FnO stocks, grouped by GICS sector, top 3 per sector by first-hour return

indicators.name: sector_avg_return_60
indicators.formula: mean(return_60bar for all stocks in same sector)

long.confirmation: stock still in top 10% after 75 bars from open

short.confirmation: stock still in bottom 10% after 75 bars from open

exit.target: 0.5% from entry for longs; -0.5% for shorts
exit.signal_exit: rs_rank drops below 70 (for longs) or rises above 30 (for shorts)

filters.time_filter: compute rankings at 10:15; enter at 10:30; exit by 14:30
filters.volume_filter: stock must have > ₹10Cr turnover in first hour
filters.trend_filter: for longs: nifty50 return from open > -0.3% (not a crash day)
filters.event_filter: skip on budget day, expiry day
other_filters: minimum 5 stocks in the sector for valid ranking

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — momentum factor is well-known but sector-relative version is less crowded

weaknesses: First-hour leaders can be driven by one-off news that doesn't persist — mean reversion takes over
Sector classification matters a lot — misclassified stocks corrupt the ranking
On days when entire market is range-bound, relative strength rankings are noise
prior_art: Intraday momentum (Gao, Han, Li, Zhou 2018) — academic evidence for first-hour return persistence
notes: Test with Fama-French sector definitions vs NSE sector indices for classification.
